entry.summary: Visa-free short stays as part of the Schengen area.
entry.max_stay: 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen area
entry.pre_arrival: None today. ETIAS is on the watch list.
entry.other: Schengen Entry/Exit System: fingerprints and photo at the border on first entry (free, nothing to do beforehand). Get an entry stamp where one is still given, and carry your passport across internal borders.

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: Slovakia's official currency is the Euro. Declare more than EUR 10,000 or equivalent funds if you're travelling between Slovakia and a non-EU country. This covers all forms of currency, not just cash. Failure to do so will result in fines. You don't need to declare cash if you're travelling to or from another EU country. ATMs may be rare in mountain areas or small villages.

consular.notes: Australia doesn't have an embassy or consulate in Slovakia. For consular help, contact the Australian Embassy in Austria.

laws.rule: Don't use or carry illegal drugs. Penalties for drug offences are severe. Possessing even small amounts of illegal drugs can lead to prison sentences.
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: It's illegal to drink alcohol in the street in Bratislava Old Town. Doing so can result in a fine. There may be exceptions for: seasonal markets outdoor seating at restaurants and bars
laws.heading: Alcohol laws

laws.rule: It's illegal to take photos of: military areas military vehicles other security-related subjects
laws.heading: Photography

laws.rule: Fines for minor driving infringements are heavy. You need to pay these fines on the spot. If you don't, officials may take your licence. Penalties for serious driving offences can include prison sentences.
laws.heading: Driving offences

laws.rule: Local authorities can ask to see identity documents at any time. Always carry your passport with you. Register with the police if you plan to stay longer than 3 days in Slovakia.
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: You can drive on your Australian driver’s licence for up to 6 months. Some car hire agencies may need you to have a current International Driving Permit (IDP). Get your IDP before you leave Australia.
laws.heading: Driving permit

meetings.detail: Business meetings are covered, without being employed in the country.
